IRL: In Real Life. OUT THERE. TOGETHER. A verified, real-name community for saying what is on your mind to the people who share your place, with a quiet safety layer, designed with women at the centre and built in phases as a final-year B.Tech project.
This build has real accounts (sign-in with your mobile number and a texted code; no password, no e-mail), a Safety Circle, an SOS, and On my way (a reminder, no tracking). Nobody can use IRL to track another person. During an SOS, your location can be saved to your own record. IRL texts your Safety Circle in an SOS only if you chose it. IRL never contacts emergency services and never records sound, photos or video during an SOS.
The order of posts on Home uses what a post contains and the interests you chose; \"Talking now\" uses how recently someone commented. It never uses how many people read or commented.

IRL is a student prototype, not a released product, and there are no final terms of use yet. It is not an emergency service: it never contacts the police, an ambulance or anyone else for you, and an SMS that was sent is not proof that it was delivered or read. In an emergency, call 112 or your local emergency number. Do not rely on IRL as your only way to get help. Terms of use will be written and reviewed before any public release.

Privacy notice for this prototype build. It describes what this build actually does. It is written by the project team, is not legal advice and is not a final privacy policy.
Who can see your data: you, and the people who run the IRL server (the project team). Nobody else can look you up, follow you or see where you are: IRL has no family, partner or guardian mode, no location on request and no remote view, by design. IRL has no advertising and no analytics, and does not read your phone\'s contacts or messages.
Account: you sign in with your mobile number and a 6-digit code texted to it; there is no password and no e-mail. The server stores your real name, your number and when you confirmed that you are 18 or older (your date of birth is checked once and never stored). Codes are kept on the server only as a one-way hash for a few minutes; wrong codes and requests are counted in the server\'s memory only. This device stores your name, the last 4 digits of your number and a sign-in token, sealed with a key held by your phone\'s secure hardware. Deleting your account, cancelling that, signing out your other phones and ending an SOS from another phone are confirmed with a fresh code texted to your number. Asking to delete your account starts a 7-day wait; after it, everything your account holds on the server is deleted (see the end of this notice).
Location: only while an emergency is active, and only if you allow it, your phone\'s location (with its accuracy and the battery level) is saved to your own emergency record on the IRL server. Only you can see the saved points; the only place your location goes beyond that is a map link in the Safety Circle texts of that SOS (see below). On my way never uses your location. Points that are waiting to be uploaded are kept in memory, not stored on the phone. Location points are deleted together with the emergency record and your account.
SOS without internet: an SOS starts on your phone at once, even without a connection, and is recorded on the server as soon as it can be reached. Until then the phone keeps only a random reference for the SOS, its start and end times and whether you tapped Call 112 (no location, no number); the server stores the reference and marks the times as your phone\'s. Signing out deletes what is still waiting.
On my way: the server stores the walk (the optional text you type, such as "Library", the reminder time, when you tapped More time and how it ended). No location, no route and no track: it is a reminder on your own phone, by the phone\'s alarm. Nobody is contacted. "Let someone know" opens your phone\'s share menu with a note you can edit; IRL does not see who you send it to.
Safety Circle texts (only if you choose "Yes, text them for me"): when your SOS reaches the IRL server, the server texts up to 5 of your enabled contacts with Indian mobile numbers, through the SMS provider Fast2SMS (fast2sms.com), with exactly this: your name, your number, the time, that you pressed SOS, a map link to your latest location, and later one text when you end the SOS. The provider sees these texts to deliver them. The server keeps for each text only the contact, the kind, the status and a one-way key of the number (never the text, never a readable number); they are deleted with the emergency and your account. Nothing is sent for an SOS ended from another phone, or one the server receives more than 30 minutes after it started. Without internet IRL cannot text anyone: you can always tap Text to send a ready message yourself from your SMS app (your contacts\' names and numbers are kept on this phone for that, deleted when you log out). "Test my alerts" texts your own number. A number can ask IRL to stop all IRL texts to it. Tapping Call 112 opens your phone\'s dialer; IRL records that it was opened, not whether you called.
Account deletion: you confirm it with a code texted to your number; it is refused during an emergency and for 24 hours after one, and it waits 7 days (cancel with a code; signing in does not cancel it). Then the server deletes your account and everything it holds: emergencies and their locations, walks and Safety Circle. If you ever acted as a moderator, your account row stays as an anonymous, switched-off record so that the moderation log keeps who decided what; your name, number and safety data are still deleted. After the deletion, this phone removes the settings it kept for the account the next time it learns of it, or when you tap the button on the login screen.
Retention in short: emergency locations and walks stay until you delete them or your account; walks keep no location; moderation log 365 days.
A complete privacy policy will be written and reviewed before any public release.

Say it true. Be kind to people.

• Harassment, insults and bullying
• Hate, including caste, religion, gender, sexuality, region or language
• Threats
• Sexual content involving others without their consent
• Sharing where someone lives or is, or who they are (doxxing)
• Posting where someone else is right now
• Spam and scams
• Pretending to be someone else

• Anyone can report a moment or a person. Nobody is told who reported.
• When several people report something on their own, it is shown collapsed, behind a tap, until a moderator from the team looks at it.
• Only a moderator can hide or remove something, or pause someone, and always with a reason you can see.
• You can ask for a review of a decision. Another moderator looks at it.
• Moderation never touches your SOS or your other safety tools: walks with check-ins and the Safety Circle.

• A private reply takes turns: one message each, then wait for an answer. Either of you can end it.
• Nobody is shown whether or when you read anything.
• Every message is checked the same way as a moment. One that may break these guidelines waits for a moderator before it is delivered; one that may hurt is shown behind a tap. You are always told.
• You can report a message in a plan or a private reply: touch and hold it. A moderator then reads that message and up to ten before it, never the whole conversation.
• The person who made a plan decides who is in. Nobody is ever told they were turned down.
